card: Logs a failure instead of returning false if re-unlocking an encrypted wallet fails during `CWallet::EncryptWallet`. Today, an unlock failure at this stage causes the `encryptwallet` RPC to report that wallet encryption failed, despite the encryption having already succeeded and been committed to disk. The author demonstrates this mismatch by simulating an unlock failure, which emits 'Failed to encrypt the wallet' on the first call and 'running with an encrypted wallet' on the second.
evidence: PR description: mutating `Unlock()` to fail in `EncryptWallet` causes `encryptwallet` to return 'error code: -16, Error: Failed to encrypt the wallet.', followed by subsequent calls failing with 'error code: -15, Error: running with an encrypted wallet'.
problem: During `CWallet::EncryptWallet`, the wallet is encrypted and written to disk before an attempt is made to unlock it to run `SetupWalletGeneration()`. If that unlock fails, the method returns `false`, causing `encryptwallet` RPC callers to receive an error that encryption failed even though the wallet is already permanently encrypted.
scope_notes: A 1-line change in `src/wallet/wallet.cpp`. Note that if unlock fails and execution continues, `SetupWalletGeneration()` will be called while the wallet remains locked.
summary: In `CWallet::EncryptWallet`, log a failure instead of returning `false` if re-unlocking the wallet with the new passphrase fails. This prevents the `encryptwallet` RPC from reporting that encryption failed when the wallet has in fact already been successfully encrypted on disk.
